_README: Visa-free-but-K-ETA-required guide: Malaysia → Korea. Visa-free 90 days, but Malaysia is NOT on the temporary K-ETA exemption list, so K-ETA must be applied for. Numbers grounded in facts.json (visa-malaysia-free, keta-fee-validity).
metaTitle: Malaysia to Korea: Do You Need a Visa? (2026) — Korea Trip Hub
metaDesc: Do Malaysian passport holders need a visa for South Korea? No — visa-free for up to 90 days. But you DO need K-ETA (₩10,000, valid 3 years): Malaysia isn't on the K-ETA waiver list. Step-by-step entry guide inside.

verdict.headline: No tourist visa needed — but you must apply for K-ETA.
verdict.sub: Malaysian passports are visa-free for short tourism, so there's no visa to apply for. But Malaysia is not on the K-ETA waiver list, so you must get a K-ETA before you fly. With a valid K-ETA you're then exempt from the e-Arrival Card.

highlights.title: No visa for up to 90 days
highlights.body: Under the Korea–Malaysia visa-waiver agreement, Malaysian passport holders enter Korea visa-free for short-term tourism and can stay up to 90 days. There is no tourist-visa application to file.

highlights.title: But you DO need K-ETA
highlights.body: Malaysia is not among the 22 countries/regions on the temporary K-ETA waiver, so you must apply for K-ETA before boarding. It costs KRW 10,000 (about US$8), is valid for 3 years with multiple entries, and is applied for only at the official site k-eta.go.kr.

highlights.title: K-ETA replaces the e-Arrival Card
highlights.body: Once you hold a valid K-ETA you're exempt from the e-Arrival Card — you don't file both. (If you're exempt from K-ETA by age — 17 and under or 65 and over — file the free e-Arrival Card instead.)

tldr: No tourist visa — Malaysian passports are visa-free for up to 90 days.
You must apply for K-ETA before you fly (KRW 10,000, valid 3 years) — only at k-eta.go.kr.
Apply at least 72 hours before departure; a valid K-ETA then exempts you from the e-Arrival Card.
Bring a passport valid for your stay plus proof of onward/return travel.

items.title: Confirm you're visa-free
items.detail: Malaysian passports enter Korea visa-free for short tourism (up to 90 days) — there's no tourist visa to apply for.

items.title: Apply for K-ETA (required)
items.detail: Apply at the official site k-eta.go.kr at least 72 hours before boarding. The fee is KRW 10,000, valid 3 years with multiple entries. Beware copycat sites that charge extra — only k-eta.go.kr is official.

items.title: Check passport & onward ticket
items.detail: Make sure your passport is valid for your stay, and have a return/onward ticket plus your first accommodation address.

items.title: At immigration
items.detail: With a valid K-ETA you don't file the e-Arrival Card. Show your passport at arrival; fingerprints and a photo may be taken. Keep it tourism — no paid work on visa-free entry.

items.q: Do Malaysian passport holders need a visa for Korea?
items.a: No — for short-term tourism, Malaysian passport holders enter Korea visa-free and can stay up to 90 days. You do not apply for any tourist visa.
Yes. Malaysia is not on the temporary K-ETA waiver list, so you must apply for K-ETA before boarding — at the official site k-eta.go.kr.

items.q: How much is K-ETA and how long is it valid?
items.a: It costs KRW 10,000 (about US$8), is valid for 3 years, and allows multiple entries. Apply only at k-eta.go.kr.

items.q: Do I also need the e-Arrival Card?
items.a: No — if you hold a valid K-ETA you're exempt from the e-Arrival Card. You file one or the other, not both.

items.q: Can I work or study on this entry?
items.a: No. Visa-free entry is for tourism and short visits only; working or studying requires the appropriate visa.
